description: Who we are Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest-growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere. About this role: We're looking for a Data Scientist to sit at the heart of how we fight fraud — building the models, experiments, and detection systems that protect millions of customers and merchants across our platform. This is a high-impact role at the intersection of machine learning, product, and engineering, where your work will directly shape how Moniepoint detects and responds to emerging fraud threats. You are a data-driven, intellectually curious Data Scientist who is energized by hard problems in fraud and financial crime. You'll prototype and ship ML models, design experiments, and uncover new fraud signals across our ecosystem — partnering closely with engineers, product managers, and analysts to turn your work into production-grade systems. Responsibilities: Prototype, evaluate, and help produce machine learning models for fraud detection; own their ongoing monitoring and retraining cycles. Design and run experiments to measure the impact of fraud interventions, balancing customer experience against loss reduction. Size fraud typologies across our product lines to inform prioritization and investment decisions. Build and maintain anomaly detection systems to surface novel fraud vectors before they scale. Work closely with fraud operations, engineers, product managers, and data analysts to translate model outputs into real-world mitigations. Experience & Background: A strong foundation in statistics with a degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science, or similar). 3+ years of experience in data science, decision science, or risk analytics within fraud, payments, or financial crime. Hands-on experience building and deploying machine learning models in a production environment. Fraud, risk, or financial services experience is a strong plus. Solid grounding in data science fundamentals: experimentation, statistical inference, model evaluation, and feature engineering. Comfort working in fast-paced, cross-functional teams with high ownership expectations. Skills & Competencies: Proficiency in Python and SQL; comfort working across the full model development lifecycle. An investigative instinct — you enjoy digging into data to find patterns others miss. The ability to communicate technical findings clearly to non-technical stakeholders and translate insights into action. What Success Looks Like in This Role: Production-grade ML models and anomaly detection systems that effectively surface and mitigate novel fraud vectors before they scale. Well-designed experiments that successfully balance customer experience against fraud loss reduction. Clear sizing of fraud typologies that effectively drives product prioritization and strategic investment decisions. Seamless cross-functional alignment where technical model outputs are consistently translated into real-world fraud mitigations. Why Join Us? Culture: We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We've built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning: We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks. Compensation: You'll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits. Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: Early Careers Talent Acquisition Specialist
description: About Moniepoint and Your Team At Moniepoint, we are on a mission to create financial happiness for every African, everywhere. From pioneering digital payments to powering millions of businesses across the continent, we build innovative, dependable products that everyday people rely on. As part of the People Team, Talent Acquisition doesn't just fill open roles; we shape how great talent discovers, joins, and thrives at Moniepoint. You'll join a collaborative, ambitious team of recruiters, sourcers, and operations specialists who care deeply about candidate experience, equity, and operational excellence. Job Purpose The Early Careers TA Specialist leads the operational delivery of Moniepoint's structured early-talent ecosystem, spanning university partnerships, campus hackathons, structured internships, and graduate conversions. In this role, you'll partner closely with the Senior TA Strategy & Enablement Manager to turn strategic vision into high-impact, repeatable programmes. You'll own the day-to-day rhythm of our campus presence and early-career cohorts, ensuring every student, graduate, and intern experiences a transparent, supportive, and inspiring journey into Moniepoint. Key Responsibilities 1. Campus Engagement & Community Presence Build and execute a clear, engaging playbook for how Moniepoint connects with university students and emerging talent through hackathons, tech talks, campus career fairs, and community hubs. Run the annual early-careers recruiting calendar, aligning outreach windows, assessment cycles, and start dates into a predictable, well-communicated rhythm. Establish and nurture long-term partnerships with universities, student societies, and tech communities across Nigeria to build balanced, diverse talent pipelines year after year. 2. Internship & Graduate Programme Delivery Deliver a structured, end-to-end internship experience—including recruiting, pre-boarding, cohort programming, manager enablement, and conversion into full-time roles. Partner with hiring managers and team leads to define project scopes, secure dedicated mentors, and ensure interns work on meaningful, real-world problems. Manage transparent, objective conversion assessments at each stage of the cohort lifecycle using structured, skill-based criteria. 3. Recruiting Infrastructure & Candidate Experience Design and manage smooth application, screening, and interview workflows for high-volume cohorts within our Applicant Tracking System (ATS). Collaborate with assessment partners and vendors to deliver fair, accessible, and bias-free evaluation stages for all candidates. Coordinate with People Operations, IT, and workplace teams to ensure seamless onboarding and Day 1 readiness for every cohort. Provide mentorship and day-to-day guidance to junior recruiters or coordinators supporting early-talent pipelines as the function expands. 4. Insights, Reporting & Continuous Improvement Track key programme metrics, including application conversion rates, cohort diversity, candidate Net Promoter Score (NPS), and post-internship retention. Gather feedback from candidates, interns, and hiring managers to simplify processes and continuously improve programme quality. Share regular progress updates and data-driven recommendations with the wider TA leadership. Qualifications 5-7 years of talent acquisition experience, with proven exposure to campus recruiting, university relations, early-career programmes, or cohort hiring. Demonstrated experience coordinating complex projects or multi-stakeholder programmes with strong attention to detail and follow-through. Practical experience using modern Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) and candidate evaluation tools. Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to connect authentically with university students and senior stakeholders alike. Solid understanding of the Nigerian higher education landscape and emerging talent communities. Preferred Qualifications Experience designing or running student hackathons, innovation challenges, or specialized STEM recruitment initiatives. Experience in high-growth technology, fintech, or fast-paced corporate environments. Familiarity with funnel analytics, spreadsheet reporting, or presentation design for leadership reviews. About You You're an empathetic communicator: You listen well, build genuine trust with students and hiring managers, and make every candidate feel valued and respected. You bring structure to complex projects: You enjoy taking multiple moving parts—dates, venues, mentors, candidate lists—and organizing them into clear, dependable workflows. You're a collaborative problem-solver: You approach challenges with curiosity, ask thoughtful questions, and work constructively with hiring managers to find solutions that benefit everyone. You care deeply about fairness: You believe great talent comes from diverse backgrounds, and you actively champion objective, inclusive hiring practices. You're human and grounded: You communicate with clarity, keep things simple, and bring positive energy and humility to your team every day. Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: Engineering Manager
description: Who we are   Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Why PolandPoland is a new and deliberate addition to our engineering map. We recently made our first technology hire in the country, and we see it as a long-term strategic location for senior hires, particularly within engineering. Joining now means joining early, and helping shape what our presence here becomes.So, now we are looking for our Engineering Managers to join us in Poland. About the role As an Engineering Manager, you will drive the successful delivery and execution of projects within your teams. You will manage end-to-end technical planning, ensuring that product requirements are translated into actionable tasks, while orchestrating collaboration between various stakeholders, including engineers, product managers, QA, and UX. This role requires a deep understanding of software design and development and the ability to plan, execute, and deliver product features in a timely and predictable manner. You will also be responsible for maintaining high technical standards, managing team bandwidth, and ensuring project milestones are met with efficiency and accuracy. What you’ll get to do Own end-to-end delivery and execution across cross-functional teams within your product area, ensuring predictable and high-quality outcomes. Evaluate business and product requirements for technical feasibility and architectural alignment, translating them into well-defined EPICs and technical user stories. Partner closely with Product Managers, UX Designers, and Engineers to continuously refine, groom, and prioritize the backlog. Plan and drive sprint execution with clearly defined goals, using project planning tools to establish timelines, delivery milestones, and surface dependencies early. Champion engineering processes and rituals that enable strong collaboration, accountability, and team efficiency. Monitor team velocity and capacity to optimize resource allocation, proactively balancing bandwidth against delivery commitments. Coordinate cross-team dependencies and stakeholder alignment to remove bottlenecks and maintain smooth execution. Stay hands-on in critical initiatives by guiding design decisions, enforcing sound design patterns, and participating in code reviews to maintain high engineering quality. Ensure robust monitoring, alerting, and observability for all owned services, consistently meeting defined SLIs and SLOs. Partner with Product Managers to define, track, and publish post-release product metrics, driving transparency and continuous improvement.   To succeed in this role, you should have Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field. 8-10 years of experience as a Software Developer, Software Engineer, or in a similar hands-on technical role. 5+ years of strong experience building production systems using Java and Spring Boot. Minimum 3 years of proven engineering leadership experience managing high-performing teams. Solid grasp of Agile methodologies, including sprint planning, backlog grooming, and iterative delivery. Demonstrated ability to translate complex product requirements into well-structured EPICs, user stories, and tasks. Strong backend engineering expertise; exposure to frontend technologies is a plus. Experience with project planning and tracking tools to visualize and manage delivery timelines. Familiarity with engineering, product health metrics, and monitoring tools to drive data-informed decisions. Hands-on capability to debug complex production issues, lead incident response, and conduct blameless RCA. Good understanding of modern deployment practices, including CI/CD pipelines, release management, and associated metrics. Ability to drive alignment across cross-functional stakeholders, both technical and non-technical. Excellent risk management, dependency tracking, and stakeholder communication skills. Proven track record of improving team velocity, delivery predictability, and engineering excellence.   Generic Skills Problem-solving: Ability to assess complex problems, find solutions, and make sound decisions. Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, including technical documentation and stakeholder reporting. Adaptability: Able to thrive in a fast-paced, changing environment, adjusting strategies as needed. Attention to Detail: Meticulous in documenting technical requirements and ensuring all aspects of a project are accounted for. Supervisory skills Team Management: Experience in managing and mentoring engineers, ensuring team growth and performance. Resource Allocation: Ability to assess bandwidth and manage resource distribution to optimize team performance. Feedback: Conduct regular performance reviews, providing constructive feedback and fostering a growth-oriented environment. Stakeholder Management: Lead project status reviews, manage expectations, and ensure smooth communication between teams and leadership. What we can offer you Culture - We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks. Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, paid leave, plus other benefits. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary phone call with one of our recruiters. A live coding and code review session. A system design and technical discussion round.  A project planning, execution, and product thinking round. A behavioral and technical interview with the hiring manager. Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.   #LI-Remote

You will work closely with our engineering teams to tell the story of what we’re building in a language that other expert engineers understand. This is a technical content execution role requiring strong, foundational engineering skills. You will translate what our engineers build and learn into high-quality narratives: the kind that earns genuine respect in engineering communities, gets accepted at top-tier conferences, and attracts exceptional engineers from around the world. The right person for this role is a skilled engineer who has found their voice as a writer and communicator; someone who can walk into a room of engineers as a peer, ask the right questions, and come out with a story worth telling. Who You Are To succeed in this role, you must have: Strong engineering capabilities: A solid background in computer science or software engineering. You have written and shipped code professionally, understand modern system architectures, and can deeply engage with complex technical concepts. Technical depth: Experience working within fintech, infrastructure, distributed systems, or high-scale engineering environments where you can comfortably read codebases, interpret technical documentation, and grasp deep architecture choices. Exceptional writing skills: Clarity, precision, and the ability to articulate intricate technical trade-offs and ideas accessibly without oversimplifying or watering them down. Proactive narrative instinct: The ability to independently dive into engineering projects, spot the most compelling technical breakthroughs or lessons, and build content around them without needing explicit instruction. Technical credibility: A genuine, firsthand understanding of what makes technical content credible, shareable, and respected by discerning engineering communities. Autonomy: The ability to manage multiple projects, technical interviews, and deadlines independently in a fully remote environment. It's a strong plus if you have: Active engineering or open-source involvement: An active presence in developer spaces, an updated technical blog, open-source contributions, or a history of speaking at engineering conferences. Developer Relations experience: Background in DevRel or managing technical communities, showing you know how to engage developers authentically at scale. Track record in technical publishing: Experience drafting accepted conference abstracts/proposals (CFPs) for recognized industry events. Multimodal content production: Experience writing technical video scripts, technical teardowns, or working alongside creative production teams. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary phone call with the recruiter A take-home assessment Panel interview Executive interview

title: Field Credit Officer (Akwa Ibom)
description: About Us:  Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest-growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere. Job Title: Field Credit Officer  Reports to: Regional Credit Manager  Employment Type: Outsourced  Work Mode: Onsite About this role:  As a Field Credit Officer, you would be saddled with the duty of onboarding and managing businesses that would access our credit products. You would be tasked with growing your loan portfolio while maintaining profitability by ensuring that all loans are repaid as and when due. As a result, you would play a vital role in the assessment of these businesses during their credit application and leverage innovative tools we have developed to help you monitor their performance during the course of the loan. You would also be responsible for making deductions from several information sources about the 5Cs of credit, with capacity, character, and capital as major priorities. Make recommendations to management before, during, and after the disbursement of a loan facility as to the best actions to be taken, considering several economic factors. Responsibilities: Identify and onboard viable businesses within your assigned geographical area to open business accounts with Moniepoint  Engage customers to ensure optimal usage of accounts to allow them to qualify for access to credit  Review and approve (or decline) loan requests by thoroughly analyzing all the data available  Embark on physical visitation to potential borrowers’ business places for evaluation of business books, taking inventory and turnover into consideration  Meet gross loan portfolio targets and portfolio profit targets by maintaining a healthy number of loan customers while ensuring that all loans in portfolio are performing  Monitor active loan portfolio to ensure continued use of business account and loan repayment performance  Perform all other credit-related functions as may be assigned by a supervisor  Experience & Background: Minimum of an OND in any business-related discipline  Minimum of 2 years’ experience in a sales role for credit products in a financial institution  Demonstrable knowledge of credit risk analysis  Good knowledge of financial analysis is an added advantage  Skills & Competencies: Apt attention to details  Proven simple/complex analytical skills  Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills  Agility and perseverance  What success looks like in this role: Consistent achievement of gross loan portfolio targets and portfolio profit targets.  Maintaining a healthy, performing loan portfolio with minimized default rates through rigorous physical visitations and monitoring.  Successful onboarding and engagement of viable businesses that actively utilize Moniepoint business accounts.  Accurate credit risk assessments based on key factors like capacity, character, and capital.  Why join us:  Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities.  Opportunity to work with Africa’s fastest-growing fintech and make a direct impact on business growth across the region.

title: Field Sales Agent (Abuja)
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: Field Sales Agent Reports to: Field Sales Lead About this role Moniebook is the business management software that helps Nigerian businesses run sales, stock, accounting, and payments from one place. As a Field Sales Agent, you will find the right businesses in your assigned area, show them how Moniebook works, and sign them up. This is a full-time, field-based role focused on driving merchant acquisition, building strong commercial relationships, and expanding our market presence on the ground. Responsibilities Visit and actively canvass businesses daily within your assigned territory. Qualify every lead before pitching using our Ideal Customer Profile (ICP). Conduct live product demonstrations and open engaging conversations by highlighting operational inefficiencies owners may not realize they have. Close deals, secure paid subscriptions, and collect payments. Hand customers over smoothly to the onboarding team for setup and implementation. Build, expand, and maintain a robust lead bank, logging every lead and field visit daily in the CRM. Consistently hit and exceed your monthly acquisition target of 10 new subscriptions. Experience & Background At least 2 years of proven direct sales or field sales experience (SaaS, FMCG, fintech, telecoms, or similar sectors). Prior experience selling SaaS products is an added advantage (training will be provided). Demonstrated track record of hitting and exceeding sales and acquisition targets. Resident in or willing to actively cover and travel across the designated coverage area. Skills & Competencies Confident, persuasive, and articulate communicator with strong objection-handling skills. High commercial acumen with the ability to navigate conversations and push deals to a successful close. Self-driven and disciplined, capable of managing routes and time effectively with minimal supervision. Strong local market knowledge, including key business clusters and merchant corridors within the territory. Tech-savvy and proficient with smartphones, mobile applications, CRM software, and routine activity reporting. What success looks like in this role Consistently meeting or exceeding the minimum monthly target of 10 paid Moniebook acquisitions. Establishing an organized, active pipel ine with 100% daily logging of visits and qualified leads in the CRM. Delivering high customer conversion rates through compelling, solution-led product demonstrations. Ensuring high customer satisfaction and minimal churn through seamless post-sale handovers for setup and implementation. Why join us Competitive base salary plus uncapped commission potential (including 25% commission on first subscriptions and recurring renewal commissions on acquired accounts). Comprehensive benefits and real opportunities for career progression within Africa's leading fintech ecosystem.  Continuous training, learning support, and professional development in sales and technology.

title: Fraud Investigation Officer
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Summary The Fraud Investigation Officer is responsible for investigating suspected fraudulent activities, identifying fraud trends, supporting fund recovery efforts, and recommending control improvements to minimize fraud losses and protect the organization and its customers. Key Responsibilities Investigate fraud cases and determine appropriate outcomes based on available evidence. Analyze transaction patterns to identify fraud trends and emerging risks. Document investigation findings and maintain accurate case records. Support fund recovery efforts by engaging internal and external stakeholders. Escalate complex or high-risk cases in a timely manner. Recommend process and control improvements based on investigation findings. Collaborate with Product, Operations, Compliance, Customer Support, and other stakeholders to resolve fraud-related issues. Ensure investigations are completed within agreed service levels (SLAs). Qualifications & Experience Bachelor's degree in a relevant field. 2–4 years' experience in fraud investigations, banking, fintech, or a related risk function. Knowledge of digital payment fraud, transaction analysis, and fraud investigation techniques is an advantage. Key Competencies Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Attention to detail and sound judgment. Excellent written and verbal communication. Ability to manage multiple investigations effectively. Strong stakeholder management and collaboration skills. High level of integrity and confidentiality. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Investigation turnaround time (TAT). Cases resolved within SLA. Investigation quality and accuracy. Fraud trends identified and reported. Fund recovery success rate. Quality of investigation documentation and recommendations.

title: Head, Group FP&A
description: Who we are Moniepoint is Africa's all-in-one financial ecosystem, empowering businesses and their customers with seamless payment, banking, credit, and management tools. In 2023, we processed $182 billion and are Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer. Job Purpose Builds and owns the Group's FP&A framework, methodology, and reporting standards, giving Group leadership a single, reliable view of financial performance and outlook across the Group's subsidiaries and business units: Moniepoint Nigeria, Moniepoint Kenya, MonieWorld and Moniepoint Technologies.This is a framework and consolidation role, not a day to day business unit finance role. Some subsidiaries and markets run their own standalone FP&A team that owns local budgeting, forecasting, and reporting for that business; this role sets the Group standard those teams work within and consolidates their output. Wherever a subsidiary or shared function doesn't yet have a dedicated FP&A resource, this role covers it directly. The intent is one Group framework, executed locally wherever a local team exists, with no duplicated effort. Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth. Responsibilities: Design and own the Group's FP&A framework: forecasting architecture, budget process, and management-reporting standards that every entity works to, including markets that maintain their own standalone FP&A team Consolidate entity and BU-level forecasts, including those submitted by markets with their own standalone FP&A team, into a single Group P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow, with a working currency toggle and intercompany eliminations Own the annual Group budget calendar and process: templates, timelines, challenge sessions, and Board approval, without taking over the local budget-building work each entity's own finance team already does Produce the consolidated Group forecast (2026-28 and beyond), reconciled monthly to actuals, with a clear bridge explaining variances Work closely with the Group Financial Controller so actuals, the consolidation, and the forecast reconcile cleanly month to month, and closing timelines support the reporting calendar Run the monthly and quarterly reporting cycles at Group level: consolidated management accounts, Board packs, and investor-grade reporting Build and maintain the Group's KPI and unit-economics framework, and ensure it is applied consistently across every entity's finance team, whether that entity has its own dedicated resource or is covered directly by this role Partner with BU CFOs / finance leads (Moniepoint Nigeria, Moniepoint Kenya, Moniepoint Technologies, MonieWorld) as the standard-setter and consolidator, leaving day-to-day local execution with them Lead scenario and sensitivity modelling for Group-level strategic decisions: new market entry, capital raises, new market expansion, licence applications etc. Set and enforce FP&A style and modelling standards across the Group (structure, formatting, sign-off, version control) Manage and develop the Group FP&A Analysts covering the subsidiaries and markets without a dedicated resource, plus central shared services Candidate requirements: 10+ years in FP&A, corporate finance, or investment banking, including experience building forecasting frameworks from scratch Proven experience consolidating multi-entity, multi-currency forecasts and management accounts Background in banking, fintech, or another regulated, fast-growth environment Advanced financial modelling skills (Excel at architect level); comfortable owning a model spanning multiple entities and currenciesACA / ACCA / CFA or equivalent Proven ability to operate effectively as a remote, senior finance leader across time zones and geographies Preffered Qualifications Experience in a high-growth African or emerging-markets fintech or bank Prior exposure to Board and investor reporting at Group level Familiarity with planning/consolidation tooling (NetSuite, Aleph, Pigment or similar) beyond Excel Experience standing up FP&A functions or frameworks during a scale-up phase, including defining where a Group function ends and in-country teams begin About you You think in frameworks. You build the system once, properly, rather than patching it every quarter You're comfortable holding a multi-entity, multi-currency picture in your head and explaining it simply to the CFO and Board You know the difference between setting the standard and doing the work. You'd rather make each market's FP&A team excellent within a shared framework than take their work off them You push back on numbers that don't reconcile, and you don't sign off until they do You're a strong people manager. You can direct analysts and get consistent, house-standard output from a small team You communicate in writing the way you model: structured, precise, no padding You operate well remotely: proactive, well-organised, comfortable driving a Group-wide process without being in the room What success looks like Group forecast is reconciled to actuals monthly, with variances explained within an agreed tolerance Management, board and investor reporting are delivered on time, every cycle, without late-stage rework Budget process runs to a fixed calendar with BU sign-off, with no material off-cycle changes BU finance leads use the Group model and house standards as their working framework, not a parallel one CFO and Group CEO treat the FP&A output as the single source of truth for decision-making What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary phone call with one of our recruiters. title: Head, Innovation Hubs
description: About us Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. About the role Moniepoint is building innovation hubs at three of Nigeria’s leading universities: Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), and Ahmadu Bello University (ABU). Each hub is a cross-disciplinary platform, open to students from every faculty. The model is cohort-based, industry-connected, and built to produce technical talent ready for the job market, across software engineering, AI, product, data science, robotics, and design. The hubs train students in applied technical skills, connect them to working engineers, product leaders, and founders, and provide a path into industry at Moniepoint, at other technology companies, or through ventures of their own. This is a building role. The hubs are entering their operating phase, and you will own the design of how they run and the teams that run them. What you will own Programme design. You will design the operating model for all three hubs from the ground up: how cohorts are structured, how learning is sequenced, what “job market-ready” means at each level, and how graduates are assessed and certified. This is not adapting someone else’s playbook. It is writing one. University relationships. You will be the primary relationship owner with the Vice-Chancellors, deans, faculty leads, and student bodies at OAU, UNN, and ABU. These are institutional relationships that require both strategic seniority and sustained presence. Cross-faculty engagement. The hubs are not engineering faculty initiatives. They are open to students across every faculty: engineering, sciences, humanities, business, design. You will design the engagement model that brings students from across each university into the hub and keeps them in it through the full cohort. Industry and mentorship pipeline. The hubs derive their value from the connection between classroom and industry. You will build and manage the network of engineers, product leaders, and founders, inside Moniepoint and beyond, who mentor, assess, and hire from the hubs. Facilitators and standard.  You will design the facilitator model, recruit the people who teach and assess, and own the standard those facilitators hold the cohort to. A single standard across all three hubs is non-negotiable; how it's delivered locally is yours to design. Infrastructure and operations. You will own the physical footprint of each hub, whether that means a buildout from scratch or working within an existing campus structure, and manage the timelines, vendor relationships, and hub-level budgets across three sites. You will define the staffing model for each hub and recruit the on-ground team that runs them day to day. Outcomes and accountability. You will set and own the metrics: graduate output, job placement, programme completion, cohort quality, employer satisfaction. Pipeline integration. The hubs are upstream of Moniepoint Academy and other talent programmes. You will design the connective tissue between hub graduates and Moniepoint’s internal pathways, so the strongest talent has a clear next step. Who you are 10+ years of experience overall, with at least 5 in leadership roles owning programmes, teams, and budgets end to end. You have built or led a technical training or workforce development programme at scale, ideally across multiple sites. You have taken something from zero to one - designed the model, hired the team, and held the standard yourself. You have held institutional relationships at senior level across universities, government bodies, and industry partners. You know how to navigate Nigerian university administration, or you have done it elsewhere and can credibly do it here. You have hired and managed technical educators, and you know what separates someone who can teach from someone who can teach to a standard. You understand what good engineering education looks like and what employers in software, AI, product, and data science actually hire for. You don't need to write code, but you need the technical fluency to design a programme that produces hireable engineers, not credentialed graduates. You are rigorous about outcomes and impatient with programmes that look good in announcements but cannot prove what they produce. Experience in edtech, developer education, university-industry partnerships, or workforce development is a strong signal. Building something from scratch and owning it through to measurable outcomes is essential. What success looks like Year one. Operating model live across all three hubs. Cohorts running on a common standard. The facilitator team hired and held to the same expectations regardless of site. First graduate cohort exited, with a clear placement record into Moniepoint and into industry. Year two. The hubs are recognised within Nigeria as the most credible cross-disciplinary technical training environment available to undergraduates. Employers, including Moniepoint, actively hire from the hubs. Cohort demand outstrips supply. Year three. Hubs producing technical talent into Moniepoint at a cost-per-hire that justifies the investment, and into the wider industry at a scale and quality that defines what a corporate-funded university programme can look like in Nigeria. Model documented and ready to expand if leadership chooses. What Moniepoint can offer you The opportunity to shape one of the most consequential talent infrastructure investments in Nigerian technology.  A dynamic, diverse, and collaborative environment where every team member's voice is recognised and valued.  Continuous learning and career growth opportunities.  Competitive salary, individual performance bonuses, and firmwide performance bonus. Company-covered health insurance plans. Pension plans. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary conversation with one of our recruiters. An interview with the hiring manager, our Head of Corporate Affairs. A case study or written exercise on operating model design for the hubs. An interview with our Group COO. A final conversation with our CEO.

title: Head, IT Audit
description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Job Title: Director, IT Audit Department: Internal Audit Reports to: Chief Audit Officer About this role The Director, IT Audit provides strategic leadership for the organization’s technology audit function. This executive role oversees comprehensive risk assessments, evaluates IT governance and cybersecurity controls, ensures strict regulatory compliance, and advises executive leadership and the Audit Committee on mitigating technology risks across enterprise infrastructure, applications, and cloud environments. Responsibilities Audit Strategy & Planning: Develop and execute an annual, risk-based IT audit plan aligned with corporate business objectives, regulatory requirements, and emerging technology trends. Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Assessment: Direct complex audits covering network security, cloud architecture (Google/AWS), identity and access management (IAM), data privacy, and business continuity/disaster recovery. Governance & Compliance Frameworks: Evaluate alignment and compliance with industry frameworks including ISO 27001, NIST, COBIT, SOC 2, and applicable data privacy laws (e.g., GDPR, NDPR). Executive Leadership & Governance: Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of IT auditors and technical specialists. Foster continuous professional development and technical proficiency. Reporting & Stakeholder Management: Present audit findings, comprehensive risk evaluations, and practical remediation plans directly to the Chief Audit Officer and Senior Executive Management. Continuous Monitoring & Analytics: Drive innovation by embedding automated audit techniques, data analytics, and continuous controls monitoring (CCM) into the overall audit lifecycle to enhance efficiency. Experience & Background 10+ years of progressive experience in IT auditing, technology risk management, or cybersecurity, including 4+ years in a senior leadership/management role. Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related quantitative discipline. Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA) required. Additional credentials such as CRISC, CISM, CISSP, or CIA are highly desirable. Deep technical understanding of cloud environments (Google & AWS), network infrastructure, database security, API, application controls, and IT General Controls (ITGCs). Skills & Competencies Exceptional stakeholder management, executive presence, oral and written communication, strategic problem-solving, and conflict resolution skills. Strong proficiency in risk assessment prowess and deep thinking. Advanced predictive & prescriptive data analytics skills. Self-driven capacity, agility, customer obsession, professional skepticism, and urgency. What success looks like in this role Establishment of a robust, proactive, risk-based IT audit strategy that protects enterprise assets and cloud infrastructure. High-performing, technically proficient IT audit team delivering clear, high-impact evaluations and actionable remediation plans. Continuous integration of automated audit controls, analytics, and full compliance with industry regulatory standards and frameworks. Why join us  Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities.  Fully remote work culture and support for professional development

title: Head of Debt Collections
description: About Moniepoint Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions and process over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. JOB PURPOSE The Head, Debt Collection is a strategic leadership position tasked with the architecture and execution of Moniepoint’s debt collection framework. The primary focus of this role is the minimization of Loss Given Default (LGD) within both the business and consumer lending divisions.   The incumbent will oversee, develop, and implement comprehensive and versatile debt collection strategies designed to manage a diverse portfolio of credit products, ranging from digital-first retail lending to large-ticket corporate financing.   Responsibilities include designing the organizational structure of the debt collection unit and recruiting high-caliber talent. Additionally, specialized expertise in debt litigation and asset recovery will be required to navigate complex cases of delinquency.   A data-driven methodology must be utilized to systematically evaluate the efficacy of recovery tactics and the performance of personnel.   Job Responsibilities  Design and implement a segmented debt collection framework — differentiated by product type, ticket size, and delinquency stage — spanning early-stage soft collections through hardcore legal recovery, restructuring, and write-off pathways. Define the org structure, recruit high-caliber talent, and stand up the operational and systems infrastructure (collections management systems, tracking dashboards, agent/dialer tooling) needed to run recovery at scale. Direct legal recovery strategy for the department — whether executed directly or through instruction of external counsel — ensuring all actions comply with applicable financial regulations and debt collection laws. Manage high-level engagements with external stakeholders, including law enforcement agencies, regulatory bodies, and external counsel, to expedite resolution of non-performing loans (NPLs). Design incentive structures and performance frameworks (KPIs, commission or fee structures) for the collections and recovery network to drive both recovery rate and cost-to-collect efficiency. Continuously train and upskill the collections and recovery network in alignment with collections  strategy and industry best practice. Own collections and recovery performance reporting to senior management, including recovery rate, cost of recovery, and portfolio-level LGD trends, and feed recommendations into credit committee decisions on write-offs and restructuring. Collaborate with credit, legal, risk, and finance to align collections and recovery efforts with underwriting standards and portfolio strategy. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in a relevant field. Minimum 7 years of experience in credit/debt recovery, including senior leadership of a recovery function handling high-value non-performing loans. Demonstrated experience across both high-ticket/corporate recovery (litigation-led, relationship-driven) and high-volume digital/retail collections (analytics-led, behavioral, tech-enabled)  Strong working knowledge of debt recovery laws, banking regulations, and court procedures in Nigeria. Familiarity with digital collections infrastructure and tactics — dialer/CRM systems, SMS/USSD/app-based nudges, propensity-to-pay scoring, and behavioral segmentation for low-ticket, high-volume portfolios. Demonstrated experience designing, building, or scaling a recovery/collections function — including org design, systems and process build-out, and team hiring. Proven experience overseeing recovery operations with national coverage, including a strong network of legal counsel and law enforcement contacts spanning all six geo-political zones in Nigeria — as opposed to experience confined to a single state or region. Excellent negotiation, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret financial and portfolio data to guide recovery strategy. Relevant Skills Loan Recovery & Collections Strategy (high-ticket and digital/retail) Credit Risk Management Data Analytics, Propensity Scoring & Portfolio Reporting Digital Collections Tools & Automation Negotiation & Conflict Resolution People & Performance Management Organisational Design & Team Build-out What we can offer you Culture -We put our people first and prioritize the well-being of every team member. We’ve built a company where all opinions carry weight and where all voices are heard. We value and respect each other and always look out for one another. Above all, we are human. Learning - We have a learning and development-focused environment with an emphasis on knowledge sharing, training, and regular internal technical talks. Compensation - You’ll receive an attractive salary, pension, health insurance, annual bonus, plus other benefits. What to expect in the hiring process A preliminary phone call with the recruiter An interview with one of our credit business leads A behavioral and technical interview with a member of the Executive team.  Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates.

title: Head of Engineering, Field Verification
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Why Spain Some of our most mission-critical team members are based in Spain, having joined us from companies like Wise and Glovo. Moniepoint is one of the largest and fastest-growing digital banks in Africa, and this is an opportunity to work on genuinely impactful problems: disrupting financial services at scale in emerging markets, and building systems and products that process hundreds of billions of dollars in transaction volume annually for tens of millions of people. So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Field Verification to join us in Spain.  About the role Field Verification is how Moniepoint knows that the people and businesses on our platform are real. Every Moniepoint customer, retail and business, requires a completed field verification as part of KYC. The platform coordinates physical, in-person checks — verifying individuals, business owners, business addresses and loan guarantors — and it serves nearly every part of the company: onboarding, loans, compliance and the fraud team. The system works today. A back office gives each business unit visibility and control over its own verification requests. A mobile-friendly web app puts the work in the hands of Field Verification Officers and the cluster leads who manage them across local government areas. An API layer lets other business units push verification requests in and receive results back by webhook, and an assignment algorithm routes each request to an officer close enough to carry it out. We want to be straightforward about the rest. This domain has never had a dedicated engineering leader, and that is the single biggest constraint on it. The team is one lean, cross-functional squad — an Engineering Manager, four engineers and a QA — carrying verification volume for the entire customer base. They have done that impressively well, but running lean means running in keep-the-lights-on mode, and a long list of things that would make this platform substantially better has been waiting for someone to own it. That list is the role. Trip and route management, so an officer can plan an optimal day across several sites rather than making a separate journey for each one — today we pay for a round trip per verification, and the logistics are nowhere near optimal. Capacity management. A native mobile app, wanted for a long time and never resourced. Liveness and identity verification tooling, exposed as APIs the rest of the business can build on. And as Moniepoint expands into markets where identity verification is as difficult as it is in Nigeria, Kenya among them, a platform that works beyond a single country. There is a great deal of room to build here. Whoever takes this on will set the direction rather than inherit someone else's plan, on a system that already carries real weight for the business. As Head of Engineering, Field Verification, your responsibilities will include: Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Field Verification platform end to end, and setting direction for a domain that has been running without dedicated engineering leadership. Moving the platform from keep-the-lights-on operation to deliberate, prioritised development. Leading and growing the existing cross-functional team, and building the organisation out as scope expands. Building the operational efficiency layer — trip and route optimisation, task allocation and capacity management for field officers. Owning the platform's client-facing surface: the APIs and webhooks that other business units integrate with, and the back office those units rely on. Delivering a native mobile experience for field officers. Ensuring verification data is structured, auditable and fit for compliance scrutiny. Building for multi-country expansion as Moniepoint enters new markets. Partnering closely with Product and with the business units that depend on the platform — onboarding, loans, compliance and fraud. Defining architecture standards, engineering processes and quality metrics, and hiring and developing engineers and Engineering Managers. Who you are You have built things yourself, and grew into leadership from there. We are explicit about this: we are not looking for someone who moved into management early and has led from a distance since. We want an engineer who became a leader. You are capable across disciplines. Backend, web and mobile. This platform spans all three and you will need credibility in each — a specialist in one layer will struggle here. You have built platforms, not just products. Systems used by several distinct groups of users and internal business units, with the flexibility to serve requirements you did not anticipate. You are a problem solver first. We would rather have someone adaptable than someone with the exact domain experience. Having built across different industries — fintech, e-commerce, logistics or otherwise — is a positive signal, not a scattered CV. You have 10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with substantial hands-on production engineering and strong backend depth. Our backend environment is Java and Spring Boot. You have at least 5 years of engineering leadership, including managing Engineering Managers. You collaborate well with product and business stakeholders, and can translate operational requirements into engineering solutions. Experience working with location and geospatial data is a strong plus, including map integrations. Experience with route, trip or delivery optimisation is a strong plus. Experience building for compliance — where data must be structured to evidence what was done and when — is a strong plus. Experience with identity, KYC or verification platforms is a plus. None of these four are requirements.   Cultural Alignment As well, we assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation. Customer Obsession: Build deep empathy for users. Solve problems intuitively, and fix root causes, not just tickets. Craft: Master the fundamentals. Reason from first principles, make trade-offs explicit, and raise the bar on quality. Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality. Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. Act autonomously within scope, remove friction, and escalate risks early. Ownership: Treat the platform as your own. Take initiative across boundaries and follow through without reminders. No Ego: Put the mission first. Share credit, welcome debate, and never protect status over team outcomes. Candour: Surface uncomfortable truths and risks early. Intelligent failure is welcome; concealment is not. Integrity: Stay truthful and ethically consistent. Refuse toxic behavior. Performance without integrity is unacceptable.   What Success Looks Like The domain has clear technical ownership and direction for the first time. The team out of keep-the-lights-on mode and delivering against a prioritised roadmap. Measurable improvement in field officer efficiency — more verifications per trip, lower cost per verification. A native mobile experience shipped for field officers. Verification data that stands up to compliance scrutiny across every business unit the platform serves. The platform ready to support a new market. A team grown beyond its current size, with a strong bench of engineers and managers. Why Join Us A genuinely greenfield mandate on a system that already matters. Every customer Moniepoint onboards passes through this platform. A lean, capable team making outsized impact, and the remit to build the organisation around them. Breadth: backend, web, mobile, location data, compliance and operational optimisation in one domain. Be part of a mission-driven company expanding access to financial services for millions of businesses and individuals. What To Expect in The Hiring Process A preliminary phone call with the recruiter. 60 minute High level System Design round with one of our Engineering Managers. 60 minute Panel Interview with 2 of our Head of Engineering leaders. 30 minutes focused on a technical deep dive into your CV and into a project or system you built in the past. 30 minutes focused on testing for leadership attributes. 60 minute Stakeholder Management Round with one of our Product Heads/VPs, focused on your stakeholder management and collaboration skills with product and business. 60 minute Technical round and Culture fit interview with our Co-founder & Group CTO (the hiring manager).

title: Head of Engineering, Rewards
description: Who we are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.  As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Why South Africa South Africa has one of the strongest engineering communities anywhere in the world, and we are deliberately growing our technology organisation in the country. We already have several team members based here. The work is fully remote, and the mission we are working on is a good deal closer to home than it is for our teams elsewhere. So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Rewards to join us in South Africa. About The Role Rewards is one of the most strategically important platforms at Moniepoint, and it is being built into a dedicated charter with its own engineering and product leadership. The platform sits at the centre of our retention strategy across a user base of approximately 23 million people. Today the platform does one thing: cashback. It works, but it has barely scratched the surface of what rewards can be, and the cashback product itself is not yet built to the depth it deserves. The ambition is to evolve it into a full rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform — and to do that across the full 360 degrees of our network. That means rewards for our business customers, rewards for our consumer customers, and rewards for the sales agents who drive our distribution. Very few companies get to design this from close to a blank page at this scale. The Head of Engineering owns that platform end to end. You will inherit a team of nine engineers, including an Engineering Manager, and build the organisation out from there — the current expectation is a minimum of three product units and upwards of 25 people, though the eventual shape is genuinely yours to define. Your first objective is to get the best possible performance out of the cashback product we already have. From there, you will work with Growth, Sales and Marketing to determine what we build for acquisition and retention, and roll it out across every customer we serve. This is a consumer-facing product engineering role, and that is the most important thing to understand about it. Rewards is won or lost on experimentation, personalisation, and the quality of the experience in a customer's hands. We are looking for a leader who has built and shipped direct-to-consumer products at scale, who is fluent in experimentation and A/B testing, and who has real depth in front-end and mobile engineering — not a purely backend platform leader. Moniepoint runs a Domain CTO model. We view our Heads of Engineering as the CTO of their domain: you own the technical roadmap, the architecture, the delivery, and the organisation beneath you. You will have full autonomy over engineering strategy, architecture, hiring, operating cadence and roadmap trade-offs. You will report functionally to our Group CTO, with a dual reporting line into the Product leader for Rewards. That second line is a delivery relationship rather than a seniority one — engineering and product are peers here, and you will build the team to full capacity together. Your responsibilities as Head of Engineering, Rewards includes: Owning the technical strategy, architecture and roadmap for the Rewards Platform end to end. Improving the performance, reliability and depth of the existing cashback product as an immediate first priority. Evolving cashback into a broader rewards, retention, engagement and personalisation platform serving business customers, consumer customers and sales agents. Building the engineering organisation from its current base - structuring product units, hiring engineers and Engineering Managers, and leading through those managers as the team scales. Establishing a strong experimentation culture: A/B testing, cohort analysis, and measurement that lets the team learn quickly what actually changes customer behaviour. Working closely with Growth, Sales and Marketing to translate acquisition and retention objectives into product and engineering initiatives. Owning the customer-facing experience of rewards across mobile and web, including how quickly and reliably customers receive what they have earned. Define architecture standards, engineering processes and quality metrics, and own the engineering health of the domain — incidents, production defects, deployment frequency, change failure rate, and developer experience. Build the platform to serve customers across multiple geographies as Moniepoint expands. Partner with Product to define the rewards-specific metrics and OKRs that do not yet exist, and hold the team to them. Who You Are  Direct-to-consumer product engineering at scale. You have built and shipped products used directly by large consumer audiences, and you understand what moves engagement and retention. This is the defining requirement of the role. Genuine front-end and mobile depth. You have led or personally built consumer-facing mobile and web experiences. A backend-only background, however strong, is not what this role needs. Experimentation and growth engineering. Hands-on experience running A/B tests, feature flagging, and measurement frameworks, and using the results to drive product decisions rather than to justify them. At least 5 years of experience managing managers — leading an engineering organisation through other engineering leaders, not a single team. Hands-on technical leadership. You are still close to the code. We expect a meaningful proportion of hands-on engineering time and technical credibility with the engineers you lead. 10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with at least 5 years leading engineering teams through growth phases. Comfort with our backend environment — Java and Spring Boot — and the ability to lead backend engineers credibly, even if it is not where your own depth sits. Experience building and scaling an engineering organisation from a small base, including hiring and developing Engineering Managers. Strong collaboration with commercial stakeholders — growth, marketing and sales — and the ability to translate business objectives into engineering work. Rewards, loyalty, gamification, personalisation or growth platform experience is a strong advantage but is not required. Fintech or payments experience is an advantage, not a requirement. Cultural Alignment As well, we assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation. Customer Obsession: Build deep empathy for users. Solve problems intuitively, and fix root causes, not just tickets. Craft: Master the fundamentals. Reason from first principles, make trade-offs explicit, and raise the bar on quality. Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality. Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. Act autonomously within scope, remove friction, and escalate risks early. Ownership: Treat the platform as your own. Take initiative across boundaries and follow through without reminders. No Ego: Put the mission first. Share credit, welcome debate, and never protect status over team outcomes. Candour: Surface uncomfortable truths and risks early. Intelligent failure is welcome; concealment is not. Integrity: Stay truthful and ethically consistent. Refuse toxic behavior. Performance without integrity is unacceptable. What Success Looks Like In The Role The existing cashback product performing measurably better — faster, more reliable, and more compelling to customers. A credible rewards platform roadmap defined with Product, and the first initiatives beyond cashback shipped. A functioning experimentation practice, where the team ships, measures and learns on a short cycle. An engineering organisation built out from its current base, with a strong bench of Engineering Managers and senior engineers. Rewards established as a measurable contributor to retention and engagement across the customer base. Clear architecture standards and engineering processes in place across the product units. Why Join Us A rare blank page. The platform exists, but almost everything it could become is still ahead of it, and you will define what that is. Direct influence on retention across a base of roughly 23 million users, at one of the largest and fastest-growing digital banks in Africa. Full autonomy as the CTO of your domain, with the backing to build the organisation you think the problem needs. Be part of a mission-driven company expanding access to financial services for millions of businesses and individuals. We look for people here who understand first-hand what it means for financial services to be difficult to access, and who want to work on problems at a genuine international scale - changing how banking works across emerging markets. So, now we are looking for our Head of Engineering, Sales Management Tools, to join us in Pakistan. About The Role Sales Management Tools owns MonieCRM, the operating system for Moniepoint's 50,000-strong sales network. This is not a CRM we bought — it is a workforce operations platform built entirely in-house for a multi-level field sales hierarchy, and it is how those teams run their day to day: the portfolio of businesses they manage, their own teams, their goals and performance, the physical and digital resources they need in the field, and an emerging AI-assisted support layer. Sixteen capabilities span onboarding and network management, pipeline and portfolio, performance and goals, compensation, and sales experience and support. A significant part of the domain moves money. The platform owns wallets, commission calculation and attribution, cashout and welfare funds for a network that drives the overwhelming majority of company revenue — which makes financial correctness, not just availability, a core engineering requirement of the role. Alongside that, the domain covers partner management, a rewards and retention platform serving tens of millions of users, and our marketing technology stack, including the engineering and customisation of Braze, the platform we use for customer engagement. The mandate is modernisation and reliability: re-architecting systems that have grown very quickly and making them dependable at a scale of more than 20 million users. This is a platform engineering and legacy modernisation challenge first and foremost, and prior CRM or SalesTech experience is genuinely not required. Who You Are  You have 10–15 years of overall software engineering experience, with at least 5 years leading engineering teams through growth phases. 5+ years of hands-on, production-level experience writing and shipping Java code as a practising engineer. This means years spent writing Java yourself, not years spent overseeing teams who write it. At least 5 years of experience managing managers — leading an engineering organisation through other engineering leaders, rather than running a single team. You have proven platform engineering experience at scale — building and running complex distributed systems, not feature delivery alone. You have navigated legacy migrations and re-architecture projects at 20M+ user scale. You have strong backend engineering skills in high-throughput, data-intensive distributed systems, and are proficient in Java and Spring Boot. You have managed and developed large engineering teams of 20 or more members. Experience building systems where financial correctness matters — commissions, payouts, wallets, ledgers or equivalent — is a strong advantage. A fintech or payments background is strongly preferred. CRM or SalesTech domain experience is nice to have and explicitly not required. Exposure to customer engagement or marketing automation platforms such as Braze is a plus, but not a requirement. Cultural Alignment As well, we assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation. Customer Obsession: Build deep empathy for users. Solve problems intuitively, and fix root causes, not just tickets. Craft: Master the fundamentals. Reason from first principles, make trade-offs explicit, and raise the bar on quality. Systemisation: Turn repeating decisions into scalable mechanisms. Reduce cognitive load and raise engineering quality. Urgency: Move with disciplined speed. Act autonomously within scope, remove friction, and escalate risks early. Ownership: Treat the platform as your own. Take initiative across boundaries and follow through without reminders. No Ego: Put the mission first. Share credit, welcome debate, and never protect status over team outcomes. Candour: Surface uncomfortable truths and risks early. Intelligent failure is welcome; concealment is not. Integrity: Stay truthful and ethically consistent. Refuse toxic behavior. Performance without integrity is unacceptable. What Success Looks Like In The Role Legacy systems modernised and re-architected, with measurable improvement in reliability and performance. Commissions and earnings calculated, attributed and paid accurately and on time, at network scale. A sales and marketing platform that scales with a rapidly growing agent network across multiple markets. Commercial teams able to move faster because the tooling beneath them is dependable. A high-performing engineering team with a strong bench of managers and senior engineers. Why Join Us Own the platform behind the commercial engine of one of Africa's largest digital banks — the system 50,000 people rely on to do their jobs and to get paid. A genuine platform modernisation mandate with the autonomy and backing to see it through. Be part of a mission-driven company impacting millions of businesses and individuals across Africa and beyond. What To Expect In The Hiring Process 60 minute High level System Design round with one of our Engineering Managers. 60 minute Panel Interview with 2 of our Head of Engineering leaders. 30 minutes focused on a technical deep dive into your CV and into a project or system you built in the past. 30 minutes focused on testing for leadership attributes. 60 minute Stakeholder Management Round with one of our Product Heads/VPs, focused on your stakeholder management and collaboration skills with product and business. 60 minute Technical round and Culture fit interview with our Co-founder & Group CTO (the hiring manager). Moniepoint is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and candidates. #LI-Remote

title: Head of Personal Banking Sales Network
description: Who we are Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa’s fastest growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of Naira’s in transactions monthly. Moniepoint is Africa's all-in-one financial ecosystem, empowering businesses and their customers with seamless payment, banking, credit, and management tools. About the Role The Head of Personal Banking Sales Network is an experienced sales professional who owns the retail sales distribution engine for personal banking. This is a network leadership role, not an individual selling role and you will be required to build, motivate and control a large independent contractor field force and the regional management layer above it. You will be measured on qualified customer acquisition and product penetration delivered at a defensible cost per unit.  Duties & Responsibilities Own end-to-end performance of the sales team: deliver the acquisition and transaction target through the field sales channel. Own agent productivity: acquisitions per active agent per month, share of field agents performing 100% vs target, and time to first sale for new agents. Own network health: active agent count, attrition, reactivation and coverage in priority cities Design and maintain territory structure, prioritising penetration in priority cities. Set recruitment targets for each city/cluster and ensure delivery versus the target. Own cost per acquisition through the sales channel, including commission, incentive and field support. Design commission and incentive structures that reward activated and transacting customers, not registrations. Ensure full compliance with all legal and regulatory requirements. Own the field sales performance routines: daily check-ins, weekly regional reviews, monthly business reviews. Requirements 10 - 15 years in field sales leadership, with at least 5 years leading regional sales leaders. Direct experience running a distributed agent, agency or independent contractor network of significant scale. Proven ownership of a commission or incentive scheme, including designing it and defending its cost. Strong command of sales analytics: funnel conversion, productivity distribution, cohort based performance. Strong people leadership skills: training, motivating and managing a large field sales team Experience operating in financial services, telecoms, FMCG distribution or another high volume regulated or semi regulated industry. Willingness to travel across regions regularly. Preferred Qualifications Experience in banking, payments or lending distribution in Nigeria. Experience in building and scaling a field sales team Familiarity with sales enablement tooling and CRM based territory management. About You You’re calm, objective, and grounded, even in high stakes situations. You balance empathy with fairness and have strong judgment on what’s “right” versus what’s “easy.” You communicate with clarity and confidence, building trust at every level. You think systemically and you see patterns behind cases and design solutions that prevent recurrence. You value compliance but see your role as enabling business success, not blocking it.
